references.text: Abraham offers hospitality by providing food to the visiting strangers, similar to Reuel's invitation for Moses to eat bread
Laban invites Abraham's servant in to eat, an example of ancient Near Eastern hospitality toward foreigners
Joseph invites his brothers to eat bread with him, a gesture of hospitality
Jethro (Reuel) eats bread with Moses and the elders of Israel, demonstrating his continued hospitality
A father urges his son-in-law to strengthen himself with bread, showing hospitality similar to that shown by Reuel
Boaz invites Ruth to eat bread with him, a gesture of hospitality toward a foreigner
The exhortation to show hospitality to strangers, reflecting Reuel's action toward Moses
A parallel about an invitation to hospitality ('Come home with me and eat') extended to a stranger that triggers a fateful event.
